purpose: Independent exact-byte rereview of the RT18 retention successor against the RT17 graph-quarantine rejection, the candidate-blind closed graph denominator, the retained 51-input RT17 boundary plus four exact RT17 lineage inputs, and the inherited EP8, D9, fixture, lease and semantic surfaces. This review does not apply, seal, freeze, integrate, demonstrate, qualify or release RT18.

scope.decisionRule: PASS requires stable exact subject bytes; all 55 transitive inputs independently hash-bound at review start and end; every retained RT17 pass; a closed fail-closed runtime edge denominator; every attack exercised from the actual returned VerifiedSemanticRTSnapshotV2 root; safe identity-cycle accounting; and zero new blocker.

scope.reviewedPurpose: RT18 claims to replace exactly RT17-PF-01-GRAPH-QUARANTINE-EDGE-SET-INCOMPLETE while preserving the independently accepted narrow EP8, D9, concrete-snapshot, fixture, lease and semantic results.

verdict.effect: RT18 must remain CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED. It must not supersede the rejected retention lineage, enter E8/OP6 or architecture-freeze bindings, discharge Phase 1A, or be used as product disposition authority.
verdict.statement: RT18 repairs the four concrete RT17 falsifiers and retains the EP8, D9, current-snapshot, fixture, lease and semantic passes. It is nevertheless rejected. Its self-declared 27-edge set is not a closed runtime graph denominator: a class metaclass, frames, generator/coroutine frames and an unrecognized runtime type all return clean while hiding a required edge. Independently, its bare integer-id cycle set loses object lifetime, allowing a later class mappingproxy with a reused id to be skipped; this produced 20/20 forbidden-sentinel escapes from the actual returned snapshot root in the final recorded run.

blockingFindings.finding: The candidate calls its authored 27 rows the exact closed semantic edge registry, but the dispatch neither traverses nor rejects several runtime values that can occur below admitted function globals/custom attributes. A forbidden identity behind a class metaclass, a frame or generator/coroutine frame is invisible. An unrecognized opaque runtime type is also accepted as a clean leaf rather than producing a named refusal. The same eight cases escape both as synthetic roots and after injection beneath an actual operation function reachable from the real VerifiedSemanticRTSnapshotV2 root.

blockingFindings.whyThisIsReachableFromTheReturn: The snapshot intentionally returns Python function operations and traverses their __globals__ and custom __dict__. A frame, generator, coroutine, async generator, custom class or opaque extension value may therefore be placed below an already admitted edge. The implementation must either traverse the complete runtime edge class or reject the unknown runtime type; silently treating it as a clean leaf is not a closed quarantine.
blockingFindings.whyAuthoredChecksMissedIt: The checker defines completeness as membership in its own 27-row registry. Deleting each authored row proves that those named rows are mandatory, not that the denominator is complete. The 72 authored cases omit all eight falsifiers. Its complete-returned-snapshot test creates a new wrapper {'snapshot': snapshot, 'activeAttacks': attacks}; it does not inject each attack beneath the actual returned snapshot graph and cannot expose missing runtime kinds it never constructs.
requiredRepair: Declare and traverse the class-to-metaclass edge.
Declare and traverse frame f_globals/f_locals/f_back and generator/coroutine/async-generator frame edges, or reject those runtime kinds with a named fail-closed finding before returning clean.
Define an exact admitted runtime-kind set and emit a named controlled refusal for every unknown non-atomic type; a registry-only unknown-edge mutation is not an unknown runtime-type test.
Exercise every edge and unknown-kind falsifier after injection beneath an actual returned operation function, with VerifiedSemanticRTSnapshotV2 as the scan root.
Add one deletion mutation for every new edge and preserve all 35 currently passing independent denominator cases.
Publish a successor and obtain a fresh exact-byte review; do not patch or apply RT18 in place.

blockingFindings.finding: The traversal records only id(value) integers in seen and does not retain the expanded objects. Several edge getters create ephemeral values, especially type.__dict__ mappingproxies. After one proxy is expanded and collected, CPython may reuse its integer id for a different later proxy. The second proxy is then suppressed as an apparent cycle before its forbidden descendants are inspected. The contract's cycle-safe claim therefore depends on an object-lifetime assumption it does not enforce.

sourceWitness.shape: queue holds (path, object, depth), but expanded objects are discarded while seen is only set[int]
sourceWitness.forbiddenCheckOrder: the reused identity is skipped before forbidden lookup or child expansion

independentFalsifier.construction: RootClass.__dict__ contains HiddenClass; HiddenClass.__dict__ contains the forbidden sentinel. The breadth-first walker creates an ephemeral mappingproxy for RootClass and later another for HiddenClass.

finalRecordedHelperRun.note: Allocator reuse is lifetime-sensitive; a helper-only count is not the authority.

finalRecordedActualSnapshotRootRun.root: the actual VerifiedSemanticRTSnapshotV2, with RootClass injected beneath one returned operation function custom-attribute map

independentFalsifier.reproducibility: An earlier full run produced 19/20 actual-root escapes; the final frozen-adapter run produced 20/20. The varying count is expected allocator behavior and does not weaken the single-escape soundness falsifier.

blockingFindings.whyAuthoredChecksMissedIt: The authored cycle case revisits the same live list while that object remains strongly reachable. It proves ordinary cycle termination only. It never creates and releases one ephemeral child before visiting a distinct later child, so it cannot exercise id reuse. Edge-deletion mutations validate registry presence and are orthogonal to object lifetime.
requiredRepair: Retain a strong reference to every expanded non-atomic object until traversal completes, for example an id-to-object table, or prove an equivalent lifetime-safe representation.
Keep the node budget based on distinct live identities without allowing reclaimed ids to suppress new objects.

Add the nested-class mappingproxy falsifier both as a helper root and beneath the actual returned snapshot root; require the candidate and independent strong-reference walkers to reach the same sentinel in every stress iteration.
Retain the existing ordinary-cycle, depth and node refusal tests.

rt17FindingRereview.reasonNotClosed: RT17's blocker was a completeness and fail-closed graph-quarantine defect, not a four-fixture checklist. RT18 repairs those four examples but its successor denominator still has clean runtime-edge escapes and its cycle representation can skip a distinct object after id reuse.

normal.summary: 55 frozen inputs read once; byte-bearing fixtures 7/2 and 5/3; exact RT13 semantic basis; authored 27-edge current graph clean; real v1.10 frozen dataclass; candidate not applied

authoredCheckerRegression.interpretation: The authored suite is internally green and the review reproduces its advertised counts. The rejection is not a regression failure inside those authored fixtures; it is caused by eight omitted denominator cases and a lifetime bug absent from the authored cycle fixture.

residuals.statement: The runtime graph denominator and identity-lifetime defects must be repaired in a successor and independently rereviewed.
CD-RT-5 remains blocked, product state remains BLOCKED_ON_PHASE_1A, and no architecture freeze or product disposition follows from the retained narrow passes.
No production byte store, liveness, fencing, persistence, transaction, durability, recovery, crash, concurrency or atomicity implementation is demonstrated.

nonClaims: A green authored checker does not close either independent finding.
A clean current concrete snapshot does not prove the graph walker complete.
A closed registry is closed only over its own declared rows unless the runtime-type denominator is independently derived.
This review does not apply RT18, update a claim register, accept CD-RT-5, seal retention, bind E8 or OP6, or qualify a product release.
